title: On the Method for Proving RH Using the Alcantara-Bode Equivalence (II)
content: The equivalent formulated by Alcantara-Bode (1993) consists in the injectivity of a specific integral operator connected to Riemann Zeta function: Riemann Hypothesis (RH) holds if and only if this operator has its null space containing only the null element. We proposed here a functional-numerical analysis method using operator’s approximations. It is exploiting the approximations positivity properties on finite dimension subspaces having their union a dense set. The strict positivity of the operator approximations on each subspace will attract the strict positivity of the original operator on the dense set provided that the positivity parameters of the operator approximations are bounded by a strict positive constant (Theorem 2). Then, from operator strict positivity on a dense set, will result its injectivity (Theorem 1). For an operator without positivity properties, its associated Hermitian can be used instead, both having the same null space. The criteria applied to the Alcantara-Bode integral operator on a specific dense set showed the existence of a bound for the positivity parameters of the operator approximations and consequently, proving the equivalent of RH.
